title: Understanding Trap Seal Protection and Siphoning
description: A P-trap maintains a liquid barrier that prevents sewer gases from escaping into inhabited spaces. However, unvented or improperly configured traps—such as full S-traps—create a self-siphoning effect. As wastewater rushes down the outlet pipe, momentum creates a negative pressure siphon that sucks the protective water seal right out of the trap body. To maintain an effective seal, ensure proper trap arm length and connect the drain to a properly sized vent pipe before it drops vertically. A properly vented P-trap guarantees safe, reliable odor protection.

Understanding Trap Seal Protection and Siphoning

A P-trap maintains a liquid barrier that prevents sewer gases from escaping into inhabited spaces. However, unvented or improperly configured traps—such as full S-traps—create a self-siphoning effect. As wastewater rushes down the outlet pipe, momentum creates a negative pressure siphon that sucks the protective water seal right out of the trap body. To maintain an effective seal, ensure proper trap arm length and connect the drain to a properly sized vent pipe before it drops vertically. A properly vented P-trap guarantees safe, reliable odor protection.
